# Manual versioning and publication

The two Actions are independent. **Bump version** takes one required
`patch`/`minor`/`major` choice (default `patch`), validates the selected branch
and commits only version sources. It never tags, builds, publishes or starts
another workflow. **Build** has no custom inputs: select the desired branch
with GitHub's built-in ref selector. It builds the immutable selected
`github.sha`; a separate Bump is not required.

## Source authority

The canonical version is strict `X.Y.Z`, without leading zeros or suffixes.
The original Bump header introduced in
`ec7b3ad4129b263861ef35d59bd6f3ce57f7f0b5` explicitly coordinates
`MARKETING_VERSION`, `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` and plist versions, despite
its marketing-only implementation. All six marketing settings and three
current-project settings must agree across Development, Deployment and
Default. `Info.plist` keeps its `$(MARKETING_VERSION)` short-version reference
and its absent optional build key.

Xcode actually copies `English.lproj/InfoPlist.strings`; its short-version
and human-readable version are also validated and bumped. Migration keeps
the existing **1.3.0** authority and only aligns the stale source-localization
tokens to it, preserving the original CR bytes and unrelated content. The
committed UTF-16 destination localization and prebuilt outputs are not source
authority and are left unchanged. Helpers preserve encodings, line endings,
file modes, references and optional absence rather than reserializing sources.
Duplicates, missing required values, unresolved references and drift stop
before any source writes.

## Guards and native policy

Bump requires its committed executable pre-push guard, rejecting symlinks,
mode changes and raw-byte replacements on every validation. It rechecks the
remote branch before editing and immediately before pushing, then validates
the actual single advertised old/new ref update. The commit is one direct
source-only child with Actions bot author/committer and the literal
`Copilot App` co-author trailer. Detached checkouts need no ambient identity.
Both `push.followTags=false` and `--no-follow-tags` prevent unrelated tags
from following the commit.

Build retains the original macOS-only topology: Mount, Default, deployment
target 11.5, the committed `a/libjsoncpp.a`, Cocoa and DiskArbitration, and
`test/Plugins/Mount.bundle`. The Windows64 stub, QuickLook and other resources
remain intact. There is no Windows build. The executable must contain exact
`arm64` and `x86_64` slices and must not contain `i386`; runtime dylibs require
both modern slices but retain the original permission for additional slices.
Cleanup is limited to proven generated leaves/intermediates, with symlink
prevalidation. Notarization requires both a successful exit and `Accepted`,
followed by stapling and strict signature verification.

The initial checkout must be clean, including ignored files. Final checks
retain native-generated bytes, including tracked built plist/localization,
and allow only explicit generated paths and narrow Xcode intermediates.
Inside `build/XCBuildData`, only `build.db`, `build.db-wal`, `build.db-shm`
and descendants of lowercase 32-hex `.xcbuilddata` directories are generated;
arbitrary source files and lookalike names remain protected.
The immutable HEAD, complete index, raw nongenerated bytes, flags and
unexpected untracked/ignored files are independently checked. Generated files
must not be staged to hide a source/index change.
Final publication also rechecks copied manifest/constants against their exact
source bytes and requires every packaged native output to remain regular and
nonempty. A migration-branch correction explicitly supplies its expected old
SHA and must be one direct child; the actual advertised old/new record is
validated before a nonforce update.

## Create-only publication and recovery

Before native work, and again after build/sign/notarize/staple, authenticated
checks read every release page through an empty page (including drafts),
strictly validate JSON/schema, inspect matching API refs and the exact Git tag
advertisement, and reject existing publication state. Explicit nonempty
`GH_TOKEN` is required. Repository-wide `release-publication` concurrency uses
`cancel-in-progress: false`; it is not a FIFO guarantee.

Publication separately creates the tag at the immutable selected SHA, verifies
it through API and Git, then creates a new public release and uploads exactly
`Mount-X.Y.Z.zip` and `Mount-X.Y.Z.dmg` to its newly returned release ID.
Release body remains empty and generated notes remain disabled, matching the
original policy. There are no updates, deletes, clobbers, reuse, rollback or
automatic retries. Any failure retains partial state and reports the tag,
release ID and confirmed/possible uploads for manual inspection and recovery.
Do not rerun an occupied version blindly; an operator must reconcile retained
state explicitly.

## Offline regression checks

Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`
and `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml`. The suite uses local bare Git,
authenticated API doubles and closed-PATH native/credential stubs; it does not
run native toolchains, signing services or 4D.

Adapted prior art is pinned to the migration's verified immutable references:
native-encoding-detection `c42ca56`, file-information `1984897`,
common-string-algorithm `2606a68`, window-button `3f14fac`,
raw-picture-data `8144537`, PRNG `522f62e`, get-file-description `0e6dad3`,
maddy `e000f17`, keychain `7aedc6b`, window-style `2794dbe`, and the mandatory
guard-integrity correction in shell-execute-v2
`ee33f21111d9a042101ccc11d68672a7a0067e9c`.
The narrow XCBuildData classifier and final resource recheck follow serial
`32f33a3b3de7dd5201b215ff6050dd3d68e03936`.
